c.tagline: Navarre's walled city of San Fermín, bull-running, and Basque-inspired pintxos.

taxi.fareNote: Metered white taxis; ride-hailing is limited, with Cabify the main app. Fares and hotel prices rise sharply during the San Fermín festival in July.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance.

avoid.reason: During San Fermín the Casco Viejo fills with drunken crowds and pickpockets, so secure valuables and skip dark side streets late.

hood_desc: The medieval walled old town and heart of San Fermín, packed with the cathedral, Plaza del Castillo, the Calle Estafeta bull-run route, and pintxo bars. The best base for first-timers and nightlife.
The elegant 19th- and 20th-century grid south of the old town, with boulevards, boutiques, the Ciudadela park edge, and upscale dining. Good for shopping and a refined stay.
A leafy, largely residential district west of the centre around the Yamaguchi park and university, calm and local. Suits families and longer stays.
A traditional neighborhood in the river bend below the walls, increasingly gentrified, with riverside walks along the Arga. Good for a local, budget-friendly feel.
A modern residential area near the university and Navarra hospital, full of everyday shops, cafes, and green space. Quiet and practical, away from the tourist core.

water.note: Tap water is safe and excellent quality.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 11 PM, with a limited night-bus network on weekends.
transit.note: Pamplona has no metro or tram; the villavesa city buses (run by TCC) cover the city and its metro area. The walled old town is small and best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash or tap a contactless bank card; a rechargeable travel card offers cheaper fares.

bus: ALSA & Conda intercity coaches from Pamplona bus station
train: Renfe services to Madrid, Zaragoza, Barcelona & San Sebastián from Pamplona station

transit.m: Taxi to city centre (~15 min; there is no regular airport bus)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill for good service is appreciated but not required.
